text:
Connor Clifton came back to Boston, where he played his first 232 NHL games, and has found himself on the margins. CBS Sports put it plainly on Nov. 13: stuck in a depth role. He has played nine of the Bruins' games, only three since Oct. 10, and both of his last two were losses, part of a three-game Boston skid.

When he plays, he plays real minutes, about 19 a night, and he leans into the physical side (25 hits in nine games). Evolving-Hockey's read on last season in Pittsburgh is the case for him: opponents got fewer chances with him on the ice (94th percentile among defensemen) against the toughest competition in the league (99th percentile). The case against is just as specific. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had only 18% of his exits keeping possession, so pressure tends to end in clears off the glass, and he takes more penalties than he draws.

So far this season the Bruins have 53.1% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on at five on five. Whether that earns him a regular spot is Boston's call to make.
